description.narrative: The Attorney-General's Department's (AGD) contribution to the Pacific Police Development Program aims to modernise Pacific island countries' policing, law enforcement and criminal justice legislation and policies. This allows police and justice agencies to respond more effectively to law and justice issues, including violence against women, corruption and transnational crime. AGD works with Pacific island countries and the Australian Federal Police to develop and implement key components of an improved criminal justice system, both bilaterally and regionally. This includes delivery of the Pacific Legal Policy Champions and Pacific Legal Policy Twinning Programs.

description.narrative: In November 2023, the Pacific Islands Law Officers’ Network’s Sexual and Gender Based Violence Working Group launched the Regional Guidelines for Prosecutors and Witness Support Officers to support Vulnerable Witnesses through the Prosecution of Sexual and Gender Based Violence Offences. The Regional Guidelines aim to support vulnerable witnesses by expediting prosecutions, reducing re-traumatisation, ensuring courts hear the best evidence and improving public confidence in reporting SGBV offences. ‍ In March 2024, implementation of the Regional Guidelines was supported by a workshop for the participating jurisdictions. A key outcome was development of tailored country specific implementation plans. To strengthen accountability for implementation, participants must undertake monitoring and evaluation on their implementation progress and provide this reporting. Participants are championing institutional changes to policing and regulations, and increasing organisational capacity to better support vulnerable witnesses.
